instruction: Create a new sheet and identify the year with the minimum Current Liabilities value, writing the year in cell A2 and the value in cell B2.

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the minimum Current Liabilities value in column F. Verified with Python: min value is 6762 in year 2014. Evaluator checks new sheet (Sheet2) for year in column A and value in column B.

scoring_breakdown.1.0: Correct year and value both written to new sheet

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is fundamentally incorrect for verification task
Getter scans column B looking for minimum value (lines 42-49 in xlsx.py) instead of reading specific cells A2 and B2
Instruction requires WRITING results to A2/B2 of new sheet, but getter tries to FIND minimum by scanning column B
Getter logic confuses data extraction (finding minimum in original data) with verification (checking what user wrote in specific cells)
The evaluator will likely fail or return incorrect results since Sheet2 should only contain data in A2/B2, not a column of values to scan through
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace getter logic to directly read cell A2 and B2 from sheet index 1 (Sheet2)
Remove the loop that scans for minimum values (lines 42-49)
Getter should return {'year': ws['A2'].value, 'value': ws['B2'].value} instead of scanning column B
The current getter logic would be appropriate for the ORIGINAL sheet to find the minimum, but verification needs to check what the USER wrote in the NEW sheet
